title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(小島正己研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Kojima Masami)
educationalGoal: In biology, the introduction of data science has begun, and life forms are images. The time has come when can be expressed as a numerical value. In our laboratory, we will acquire such cutting-edge science. Continue researching the brain while wearing it. Specifically, the mechanism of nerve cells that support the function of the brain, the health of nerve cells. We would like to send young human resources to the cutting-edge biotechnology industry.
advice: The functions performed by living organisms are controlled by proteins with various functions. In this course, we will understand the role of proteins in living organisms through molecular biology and cell biology of the neurotrophic factor BDNF.
books: Molecular Biology of THE CELL Sixth Edition
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable to understand the basics of experimental methods, principles of equipment used, reagent adjustment methods, biology, physics, medicine, statistics, etc. Actively make daily experiments and presentations at seminars. In the seminar, report the research results and discuss them. Furthermore, amend the research plan for the purpose of research. It is important to be able to do these things.

activityGoals.body: Life phenomena can be grasped through observations, experiments, and discussions rather than letters.
Understanding life phenomena at the molecular and cellular level can be done through experiments.
Explain how the integrated function of the brain works.
Able to write reports and dissertations on the findings.

achievementLevels.ideal: To have a cooperative attitude that values teamwork and enables overall results. Summarize the research results as a graduation thesis. Being able to logically explain the research content to a person with various knowledge.
achievementLevels.standard: Make a research plan from a literature search. Work on the experiment and summarize the results. More importantly, it is possible to argue that the results can be interpreted. Being able to summarize the research content in a graduation thesis and announce the content.
